messages:
alex: starting config-only deploy: thin fallback routing + soft throttle. canary to 2% for 15m.

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy 3490012345 by alex. canary: routes=thin-fallback-3, throttle=soft-0.85

jamie: quick check — what's the exact throttle param? can we log token-level drop?

alex: using `rate_limit_percent: 85` (soft) + `max_concurrent: 120` per pool. tiny batch window 20ms.

sasha: ack. Observability hooks: please enable `emit.fallback_reason` and `qps.sampler=10%`

alex: yes added. config snippet:
```
routing:
  policy: thin_fallback
  fallback_variant: v2-small
throttle:
  kind: soft
  pct: 85
batching:
  target_ms: 20
```

ryan: watch for 504s — if latency p50 > 300ms or 5xx spike >0.3% we rollback.

deploy-bot: canary started — 2% traffic, group=redwood-canary-38. Monitor channel: #eng-sre

sasha: seeing slight tail latency bump on shard 7, +40ms. Not alarming yet.

jamie: traffic shaping looks fine. No errors in canary logs.

alex: hold for 15m then ramp to 20% if stable. Manual hot-rollback plan: `kubectl -n inference set image ...` documented in runbook.

ryan: if errors cross threshold or user-facing error rate >0.25% for 10m, initiate rollback and pin routing to `v1-stable`.

sasha: noted. I put alert in paging rule: `if http_5xx_rate > 0.25% for 10m then page oncall`.

alex: post-mortem: collect sample prompts, and ensure cache warmup persisted. We'll tag release notes with `config: thin-fallback soft-throttle`.

jamie: all good from my side. keeping eyes on dashboards.

alex: thanks — keeping this thread as source-of-truth. :thumbsup:
